Detailed Description

A base class for the various forms of Constants that will represent data types.

Each type has 0, 1, or 2 underlying types:

  • A TerminalTypeConstant has no underlying type(s); it is a terminal;
  • Type constants that modify a single underlying type include ImmutableTypeConstant, AccessTypeConstant, ParameterizedTypeConstant, and AnnotatedTypeConstant; and
  • Type constants that relate two underlying types include IntersectionTypeConstant, UnionTypeConstant, and DifferenceTypeConstant.

There are number of TypeConstant transformation APIs. If a transformation is based only on the state of the TypeConstant itself, it doesn't require passing a target ConstantPool, since the transformed constant doesn't create any new cross-pool dependencies and can be safely placed into the same constant pool.

◆ combine()

TypeConstant org.xvm.asm.constants.TypeConstant.combine ( ConstantPool pool,
TypeConstant that )

Produce a minimal representation of a type that is known to be assignable to both this and the specified type.

The resulting type is guaranteed to be the same or narrower than this type.

Note: while this operation is most of the time commutative, e.g. t1.combine(t2) === t2.combine(t1) there are some dynamic type scenarios where both t1.isA(t2)==true and t2.isA(t1)==true, but still one time is more descriptive that another and the way combine() is called may be significant.

◆ ensureVirtualParent()

TypeConstant org.xvm.asm.constants.TypeConstant.ensureVirtualParent ( TypeConstant typeParent,
boolean fPromote )

Replace this VirtualChild's parent with the specified parent type.

Consider the following class inheritance diagram: 

   B.C0 <- D.C0
    ^
   B.C1 <- D.C1

When a super type for D.C1 is calculated by isA() and createContributionList() logic, the resulting type need to "retain" the origin parent type. That retained parent type is then used by the same logic to calculate the super type of B.C1 not as B.C0, but as D.C0 instead!

Parameters
typeParentthe new parent type
fPromoteif true, the new VirtualTypeConstant should have its parent to be the specified parent type; otherwise the parent type should be simply retained by the new VirtualTypeConstant
Returns
a new VirtualChild type that has the specified parent type

◆ getCanonicalJitType()

TypeConstant org.xvm.asm.constants.TypeConstant.getCanonicalJitType ( )

Canonical JIT type for an arbitrary Ecstasy type represents a type that JIT compiler uses for variables and properties that hold non-primitive instances of the corresponding type.

The cannonical type is always either TerminalTypeConstant with a isSingleUnderlyingClass or a ParameterizedTypeConstant with non-parameterized canonical types as parameters.

The following should hold :

  • for any type T, T is-a C(T)
  • if T2 is-a T1, then C(T2) is-a C(T1)
  • for any type T, the JitClassName(T) == JitClassName(C(T))

For every non-parameterized type of single underlyin class (regardless of access and immutability modifications) the canonical type is the corrsponding TerminalTypeConstant.
For a parameterized type with parameters of non-primitive types with trivial constraints, the canonical type is also the corrsponding TerminalTypeConstant; otherwise it s the parameterized type with parameters of primitive or constraint types.
For union or difference types, the canonical type is ConstantPool#typeObject().
For intersection types, it's the most specific canonical type across the contributing types.

Returns
a canonical Jit type where all the type parameters are either primitive types or corresponding formal type constraint types

Reimplemented in org.xvm.asm.constants.CastTypeConstant, org.xvm.asm.constants.IntersectionTypeConstant, org.xvm.asm.constants.ParameterizedTypeConstant, org.xvm.asm.constants.RelationalTypeConstant, and org.xvm.asm.constants.TerminalTypeConstant.

◆ getGenericParamType()

TypeConstant org.xvm.asm.constants.TypeConstant.getGenericParamType ( String sName,
List< TypeConstant > listParams )
protected

Find the type of the specified formal parameter for this type.

Note, that this method is used to find a non-contradictory potential compile-time resolution rather than a guaranteed run time one.

For example: given a type: String[]? it's natural to decide at compile time that the type for the "Element" formal name is String. However, at run time the answer may differ.

Parameters
sNamethe formal parameter name
listParamsthe list of actual generic parameters
Returns
the corresponding actual type or null if there is no matching formal type

◆ isContravariantParameter()

boolean org.xvm.asm.constants.TypeConstant.isContravariantParameter ( TypeConstant typeBase,
TypeConstant typeCtx )

Let's assume the following:

  • there is a method M2 on a class C2 represented by type "typeCtx" that has a parameter of this type;
  • there is another method M1 from a class C1 that is present as a contribution to C2, that has the same name, same number of return values and parameters as M2 and a corresponding parameter of the "typeBase" (C1).

Determine whether M2 could be invoked via a signature of M1, and M2 could then "super" to M1.

Note: despite the name this method also handling the auto-narrowing covariance.

Parameters
typeBasethe type to determine the contravariance with
typeCtx(optional) the type within which context the covariance is to be determined

Reimplemented in org.xvm.asm.constants.TerminalTypeConstant.

◆ isCovariantReturn()

◆ isPhantom()

boolean org.xvm.asm.constants.TypeConstant.isPhantom ( )

A virtual child type is said to be a "phantom" if it represents a child with a non-existing structure.

For example, let's say we have classes:


  class B
      {
      class C // child of B
           {
       }
  }
  class D
      extends B
      {
  }

In this case virtual child type VCT(D, "C") is a phantom virtual child type, but VCT(B, "C") is not.

Returns
true iff this type represents a phantom virtual child

Reimplemented in org.xvm.asm.constants.VirtualChildTypeConstant.

◆ m_cInvalidations

transient volatile int org.xvm.asm.constants.TypeConstant.m_cInvalidations
private

The last time that we checked the invalidations from the ConstantPool, we cached the number of invalidations that had been done up to that point in time.

This is that number. This gives us a very quick way of verifying that no new invalidations have occurred. This value could be higher than the value in the TypeInfo, which represents the number of invalidations that had been done before we started to create the TypeInfo.
